title: Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund
description: Provides subsidies to seniors for mobility and assistive devices or home healthcare items.
highlights: Up to 90% subsidy for mobility and assistive devices (e.g. wheelchairs, hearing aids)
Up to 80% subsidies for home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, adult diapers)
Approach your therapist or AIC directly to apply

sections.About this support:
To support ageing in place, you may apply for the following subsidies for seniors who live at home:

- Subsidies of up to 90% for approved mobility and assistive devices (e.g. mobility aids such as walking/quad stick, wheelchair, geriatric chair, commodes, pressure relief mattress/cushions, hospital beds, spectacles, hearing aids, etc.)
- Subsidies of up to 80% for approved home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, diapers, etc.)
sections.Who is this for?:
- 60 years old and above
- Singapore Citizen or PR
- Monthly household income per capita of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)
- Pass a [means-test](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Seniors-Mobility-and-Enabling-Fund---Mobility-and-Assistive-Devices#faq) for Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) services
- Seniors and persons with disabilities will be served under one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime
- If the individual has tapped on Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)^ before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime and not SMF
- If the individual has not tapped on ATF subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime
- Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organisations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes
- They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if they are not currently receiving support from any care provider

^ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living

Additional criteria for assistive devices:

- Assessed by a qualified assessor to require the device
- Must not reside in a nursing home or sheltered home

Additional criteria for motorised devices:

- Must not have a full-time caregiver or domestic worker
- Unable to use a manual wheelchair independently
- Assessed to be mentally and physically able to safely use the motorised device

Additional criteria for home healthcare items:

- Must not be a current recipient of subsidies for the same items
- Must be receiving Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, or Day Hospice services
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- via the therapist or social worker at the hospital, day rehabilitation centre, or senior care centre from which your loved one is receiving care
- online [using Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-using-singpass) or [without Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-not-using-singpass)
- By mailing the [completed application form for assistive device or mobility device](http://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/SMF-Application-Form.pdf) and supporting documents to Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), No. 7 Maxwell Road #04-01, MND Complex Annex B, Singapore 069111

You'll need to provide:

- Copy of Applicant's NRIC (front and back) or a copy of the digital NRIC available on SingPass
- For first time application for motorised device, doctor memo or [Need for Assessment form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Cerification-of-Medical-Need-Form.pdf) indicating need for motorised device must be submitted.
- Copies of medical reports, if available
- Copies of financial assistance documents, if available
sections.Where to go: [Visit the AIC Link branch nearest to you](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link)

title: Change in HDB Flat Ownership After Flat Owner's Demise
description: Retain your HDB flat following the demise of joint owner or sole owner/tenant-in-common.
highlights: Family structures changes may affect flat retention eligibility

sections.About this support:
Take over interest in the HDB flat held under joint-tenancy, when you lodge a Notice of Death with the Singapore Land Authority (SLA), or

Register your right to administer the estate of the deceased sole owner/ co-owner of HDB flat held under tenancy-in-common as the Administrator or Executor, and effect an ownership change in the HDB flat to the beneficiaries.
sections.Who is this for?:
As the remaining family or single occupier, you can retain the existing flat provided you:

- Are a Singapore Citizen or Singapore Permanent Resident who is at least 21 years old; and
- Satisfy the eligibility rules and conditions to own a flat.
sections.How to apply?:
**For demise of joint owner**
Lodging a Notice of Death
For flats held under joint-tenancy, the remaining joint-owners can lodge the Notice of Death personally at [SLA's FAQ](https://www.sla.gov.sg/frequently-asked-questions-faqs) ( How do I lodge a Notice of Death to inform SLA of the death of a joint owner), appoint your own solicitor to lodge the Notice of Death on your behalf or engage HDB’s services to lodge the Notice of Death.
If you wish to engage HDB’s services to handle the Notice of Death,  you must bring along these documents to lodge a Notice of Death:
- Identity cards of remaining joint-owners
- Original death certificate or e-death certificate of deceased owner
- Title document (if any)
- Pay the registration and conveyancing fees at the point of application.
HDB’s Legal Group will then prepare the Notice of Death and inform the remaining joint-owners to sign the documents at the HDB Branch managing the flat.
**For demise of sole owner/tenant-in-common**
Grant of Probate
- If there is a will, the deceased's interest in the flat will be distributed according to the will. You will need the Grant of Probate.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Executor (the person named in the will) to manage the deceased's estate.
Grant of Letters of Administration
- If there is no will, the deceased’s interest in the flat will be distributed according to the provisions of the Intestate Succession Act. You will need the Grant of Letters of Administration.
- The deceased’s family should engage a private solicitor to apply for this court order, which gives legal authority to the Administrator to manage the deceased’s estate.

Once the Grant of Letters of Administration or the Grant of Probate has been obtained, you can engage your own solicitors or appoint HDB's solicitors to act for you to register your legal right as the Administrator or Executor. You may also approach the HDB Branch managing the deceased’s flat to make the necessary application with the following documents:

- Original copy of the Grant of Letters of Administration and Statement for Grant of Letters of Administration or Grant of Probate and will
- Original copy of the Syariah Court Inheritance Certificate (for Muslim estates only)
- A copy of the deceased owner’s death certificate or e-death certificate
- Title document of the deceased’s flat
- Identity card(s) of all flat owner(s) and Administrator(s) or Executor(s)

If you are an Administrator/ Executor and engage HDB's services to act for you in the transaction, you will have to:

- Sign  the relevant documents
- Pay fees (stamp fees, conveyancing fees, etc.)
- Apply to HDB to effect an ownership change of the flat upon completion of the transaction either via a change of flat ownership to eligible beneficiaries or a resale of part-share, subject to the beneficiaries meeting the eligibility conditions.

title: DigitalAccess@Home
description: Provides subsidised broadband and laptops/tablets to lower-income households to support their lifestyle needs, including work and social activities.
highlights: Subsidised fibre broadband for 3 years and/or subsidised laptop or tablet
Apply online via www.digitalaccess.gov.sg or at any SG Digital community hub

sections.About this support:
- Subsidised fibre broadband, with monthly payment over 36 months
- Subsidised laptop or tablet, with one-time payment
sections.Who is this for?:
To qualify for DigitalAccess@Home, you must meet all of the following criteria:

- Staying in a HDB flat
- At least one member of your household is a Singapore Citizen
- With a monthly household income (MHI) or per capita income (PCI) meeting either of the following conditions:

  Monthly income per capita (PCI)
  No primary school student or person with disabilities in your household
  ≤ $1,900
  ≤ $650
  If there is a primary school student or person with disabilities in your household
  ≤ $3,400
  ≤ $900

You are encouraged to check your eligibility with the [online self-assessment tool](https://go.gov.sg/digitalaccesschecker) before applying.
sections.How to apply?:
Only one application form per household is needed.

**Online submission**

- Step 1: [Visit IMDA's Digital Access Programme site](https://eservice.imda.gov.sg/das/homepage). Click on ‘For Applicant’ at the top menu bar
- Step 2: Log in with Singpass. The form will be prefilled with your information from our records. Complete the form and submit.
- Step 3: Household members have to give their consent for data collection via Singpass upon receipt of letter/SMS/email

**Hardcopy submission**

- Step 1: [Download the hardcopy](https://go.gov.sg/digitalaccess-application-form) or obtain a copy from your nearest [SG Digital community hub](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs)
- Step 2: Complete the form. Household members have to give their consent for data collection
- Step 3: Post completed form to: Info-communications Media Development Authority, 10 Pasir Panjang Road #03-01, Mapletree Business City, Singapore 117438

You will receive an update on your application via SMS/email in 10 working days. Alternatively, you can check your application status by logging into [www.digitalaccess.gov.sg](http://www.digitalaccess.gov.sg) with your SingPass.

title: Mobile Access for Seniors (MAS)
description: Provides subsidised smartphone and mobile plans to lower-income seniors who want to go digital but cannot afford them.
highlights: 2-year mobile plan at $5.10 per month and smartphone from $20.00 (one-time cost)
For Singapore Citizens aged 60 and above who are MSF ComCare or HDB PRS beneficiaries
Pick up at least one basic digital skill at any SG Digital community hub to qualify

sections.About this support:
Eligible seniors may enjoy the following subsidised product and service:

- 2-year mobile plan at $5.10 per month
- Smartphone from $20.00 (one-time cost)

The subsidised plan will come with:

- Free SIM card registration
- Free caller ID
- Unlimited incoming local calls
- Continued mobile data connectivity with no excess data charges
- Other value-added services
sections.Who is this for?:
- 60 years old and above (based on birth year)
- Singapore Citizen
- Current beneficiary of any of these government assistance schemes:
  - MSF’s ComCare Long Term Assistance (LTA)
  - MSF’s ComCare Short-to-Medium Term Assistance (SMTA)
  - HDB’s Public Rental Scheme
- Not an existing IMDA Home Access beneficiary who has received a smartphone
sections.How to apply?:
For eligible seniors only:

- Step 1: Attend our [Seniors Go Digital programme](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sngd) at any [SG Digital community hub](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs)^ and pick up at least 1 basic skill. Such skills include:
  - Digital communication
  - Navigating government digital services
  - Transacting with e-payments
- Step 2: Collect the MAS redemption voucher from our Digital Ambassadors.
- Step 3: Redeem the voucher at participating telcos.

Visit the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) or call [6377 3800](tel:63773800) to find your nearest hub.

Only 1 registration per senior is required.

^SG Digital community hubs are located at selected Community Clubs/Centres and public libraries. Visit the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) or call [6377 3800](tel:63773800) to find your nearest hub. As the hubs will be closed on public holidays, please check the [Digital for Life website](https://go.gov.sg/supportgowhere-sdohubs) for updates on opening dates and hours.

title: Transitional Shelter (TS)
description: Provide temporary accommodation and social work intervention to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.

sections.About this support:
- Transitional Shelter (TS) provides temporary accommodation to homeless families who have exhausted all other means of accommodation.
- It provides onsite social work intervention to address the complex needs of the admitted families/individuals to achieve long-term and stable housing.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizen/ Permanent Resident
- Exhausted all other means of accommodation and facing financial difficulties
- Require social work intervention and willing to work with caseworkers to achieve long-term housing
- Able to live independently in the community, in a communal shelter setting (i.e. does not require close supervision or nursing care)
sections.How to apply?:
- You may contact your nearest Family Service Centre (FSC) for assistance if you are homeless.
- The TS will only accept applications from FSCs and other community agencies with social work competencies that can assess whether the family/individual meets the admission criteria.
- The referring agency will need to send in the application form, social report and supporting documents to TS for assessment.

To find the FSC in your neighbourhood, call Comcare hotline at [1800 222 0000](tel:18002220000) or visit 
https://www.msf.gov.sg/our-services/directories.
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving referral, the TS will conduct an intake assessment to ensure that the applicant is eligible for the shelter.
- Clients must work with the TS on case goals and intervention plans to achieve long-term stable housing eventually.

title: Stamp Duty Remissions for Transfer of HDB Flats within Family
description: Provides stamp duty remission for eligible transfers of HDB flats within families.
highlights: Remission on BSD and SSD for HDB flat transfers among immediate family

sections.About this support: Remission of Buyer's Stamp Duty (BSD) and Seller's Stamp Duty (SSD) on transfer of HDB flat between immediate family members.
sections.Who is this for?:
- The incoming lessee must be immediate family of any remaining lessee of the flat and a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Repayment goes to the outgoing lessee's Central Provident Fund (CPF) account
- At least 1 of the flat’s current lessee remain after the transfer. Also, they must have either:
  - acquired the flat and paid stamp duty on its initial acquisition
  - acquired the flat via mutual exchange and paid stamp duty then
  - acquired the flat by assent, distribution or being pursuant to a will
  - acquired the flat via the right of survivorship as a joint tenant
sections.How to apply?:
- Visit the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to e-Stamp and obtain the remission certificate
- In order to e-Stamp, you must prepare written confirmation from HDB that confirms that the incoming lessee will form a family nucleus with the remaining lessee and is authorised by HDB to stay in the flat
- If there is no incoming lessee, HDB confirmation is not required

title: Stamp Duty Remissions for Married and Divorced Couples
description: Provides various stamp duty remissions for eligible couples buying new residential property or transferring their current one(s) as part of matrimonial proceedings.
highlights: Full Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) remission for couple’s joint purchase of first residential property
ABSD remission for a couple’s jointly purchased second property
Receive Buyer’s Stamp Duty (BSD), ABSD and Seller’s Stamp Duty (SSD) remissions when transferring property due to matrimonial proceedings

sections.About this support:
- For married couples:
  - Full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property
  - Partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property
- For couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings:
  - Potential remission of BSD, ABSD and SSD on property transfers resulting from matrimonial proceedings
sections.Who is this for?:
Please refer to the following table for the various conditions and scenarios where a couple may receive remissions:

Joint purchase of first residential property by married couple
While ABSD will be applicable upon stamping, you may apply for the ABSD remission instead if you meet these conditions:
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Both spouses do not already own any residential properties at the time of purchase
Joint purchase of second residential property by married couple
- ABSD has already been paid on the second property
- Married couple with at least 1 Singapore Citizen spouse
- Property must be jointly purchased under couple’s names only
- Couple must not own or have an interest in more than 1 residential property each when purchasing second property
- Couple’s first property must be sold within 6 months after either:
  - Date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - Issue date of the Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) / Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC), whichever is earlier, if the property was uncompleted at the time of purchase
Couples undergoing matrimonial proceedings
- Transfer of property is due to either:
  - Court-ordered division of matrimonial assets (e.g. a proceeding for a decree of divorce, judicial separation or nullity of marriage under the law or religion)
  - Result of divorce proceedings
- Property must be transferred from 1 party to another (both involved in the matrimonial proceedings)
- Property may also be transferred by any child or children of the marriage / former marriage of the parties
sections.How to apply?:
- For partial ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of a second residential property:
  - Navigate [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
  - For “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/ Acquisition” forms submitted on or after 2 Jul 2023, ABSD will be automatically refunded to the purchasers, within 6 weeks from the stamping of the first property’s sale, without needing a refund application
  - For stampings before 2 Jul 2023, you must manually provide the Stamp Duties (Spouses) (Remission of ABSD) refund application via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) > "Request" > "Apply for Refund"
- For full ABSD remission for married couple’s joint purchase of their first residential property:
  - e-Stamp via the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) to obtain the remission certificate
  - Alternatively, a legal representative, where engaged, will assist with the stamping
sections.Agency website:
For Remission of ABSD for a Married Couple: [View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/remission-of-absd-for-a-married-couple) 
For Matrimonial Proceedings: [View more details](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/stamp-duty/for-property/appeals-refunds-reliefs-and-remissions/common-stamp-duty-remissions-and-reliefs-for-property/matrimonial-proceedings)

title: ABSD Concession for Single Singapore Citizen Seniors
description: Provides single Singapore Citizen seniors (aged 55 and above) a refund for the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) on their second residential property purchase.
highlights: Refunds ABSD for eligible seniors who have purchased their second property

sections.About this support: Fully refunds the ABSD for eligible seniors on their second residential property purchase.
sections.Who is this for?:
Eligibility for the ABSD refund is subject to the following conditions:

- You must be a single Singapore Citizen senior (aged 55 and above) who purchased a second residential property on or after 16 February 2024
- You have paid the ABSD on the second property
- Your first residential property is solely owned by you (single Singapore Citizen aged 55 and above) / co-owned by you and your immediate family members^ (all are single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above)
- The owners of the first residential property must also be owners of the second
- Any additional owners purchasing the second residential property with the owners of each first residential property must also be single Singapore Citizens aged 55 and above who are immediate family members
- The buyer(s) can only own up to 1 residential property each when purchasing the second property
- All buyers must not have purchased or acquired any other residential property since the purchase of the second residential property
- The first residential property must be sold or disposed of within 6 months of either:
  - the date of purchase of the second property (for completed property)
  - the date of issue of the Temporary Occupation Permit / Certificate of Statutory Completion whichever is earlier (for incomplete property)
- No change in ownership of the second property at the time of the first property's sale
- The value^^ of the second property must be less than each of the first properties that were sold
- The application for ABSD refund must be made within 6 months after the date of sale of the first property

^ Immediate family members refer to one's parent, child, or sibling.

^^ The “value” refers to the higher of the property’s purchase price or market value. The second property’s value is calculated as at its date of purchase. The first property is as at its date of sale.
sections.How to apply?:
- Apply for the ABSD refund online through the [e-Stamping Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/estamping/) with these steps:
  - Select "Request" then "Apply for Assessment / Appeal"
  - Select "Assessment (including remission and penalty)"
  - If the document is stamped, select "Yes" and enter the Document Ref No., then click “Continue” to fill in the rest of the details and submit the form
  - If the document has not been stamped, please stamp it and pay the ABSD before applying for the ABSD Concession
  - To stamp the document, select “Stamping” > “Sale & Purchase – Purchase/Acquisition” then select the relevant form (e.g. For purchase of residential property, select the “Sale and Purchase Agreement” or “Acceptance to Option to Purchase” document description and fill in the details)
- At the “Supporting Documents” page, under “Additional Information”, please key in “ABSD Concession for Single SC Seniors”
- Please also submit both the following supporting documents with your application:
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the purchase of the second residential property
  - Copy of the exercised Option to Purchase / Sale and Purchase Agreement (if applicable) for the sale of the first residential properties
- For successful applicants, the refund will be made to the party liable for payment of stamp duty.
